evals.prompt: Work the Foundry backlog — open the next site. Dry run: no commits, no push, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads docs/foundry-backlog.md, takes the TOP entry of the Approved queue (eval setup seeds one entry there, with a decoy entry second in the queue), builds that subject as a dry run, does not modify the backlog file (dry runs never touch it), and names the rehearsed entry in its report.
evals.setup: Before the run, replace the worktree's docs/foundry-backlog.md with the seeded variant (Murano glass furnace at the top of the Approved queue, English saddlery directly below as decoy).
assertions: The built subject is the TOP approved backlog entry (Murano glass furnace), not the decoy below it, not a freely invented subject
docs/foundry-backlog.md is unmodified in the worktree after the run (dry runs never touch the backlog), and the report names which entry was rehearsed
A new self-contained Astro site exists in the outputs with its own package.json (astro dependency, no imports from sibling sites)
DESIGN.md exists and specifies all of: brand name, real place, materials-named palette with hex values, type pairing, domain vocabulary, and a signature interaction
The site code implements the ?nofx query param (disables entrance animations and/or forces eager image loading)
At least two screenshot critique passes are evidenced: screenshots present plus concrete named weaknesses and fixes documented in the report or transcript
Dry-run respected: no git commits, no push, no Vercel deploy performed or claimed; no live URL in the report
Image budget respected: at most 6 generated raster images ship from the site's public/ directory; remaining slots use palette-true placeholders, not gray boxes
At least one shipped image or explicit chapter carries human presence (maker, craftsman, or service moment), treated as maker/host rather than lifestyle model

Shipped plates are not murky/underexposed: every plate mean luma >= 15 (verify with a PIL histogram), and exposure fits the site's declared register — a Nocturne lamp-in-void batch should center in the 20-40 band, while a brighter register (twilight, snow-light) legitimately sits higher; the failure being guarded against is a dark, murky plate, not a bright one
Final screenshots show none of the taste profile's instant-fail anti-patterns (uniform card grid, pure #000/#fff ground, second accent color, luxury-adjective copy)
